cases.finding: DPBench directly exercises simultaneous shared-resource contention and coordination failure, but supplies the multi-agent organization, action protocol and communication structure itself. Published model/provider runs are not native canonical-harness S2 observations.

STALE isolates semantic interference among parallel coding workers by reusing exact solo patches and counting only tests that pass under each patch alone but fail when the patches are composed. Its controlled visibility/communication conditions supply an explicit attenuation witness: a precise message describing the finalized concurrent change reduces synthetic interference by about 98%, while real-derived Django tasks show high blind interference and substantial one-message recovery. The parallel-work and information-sharing organization is benchmark-defined, so mini-swe-agent, OpenHands and other task-solving harnesses used underneath do not own this S2 path and no canonical S2 observation is admitted.

The native historical Magentic-One orchestrator ablation removes progress tracking, loop detection and explicit direction and changes end-task performance, but the benchmark tasks do not directly instantiate an S2 disturbance and the ablation spans both S2 and S3 mechanisms. Numeric results live only in the shared raw observation record.

MAFBench includes conflict-avoidance, matching, leader-election and consensus tasks, but its published topology implementation builds the coordination application itself and currently uses LangGraph as the runtime. Canonical LangGraph has S2=—, so these runs are not LangGraph.S2 evidence.

The benchmark varies coordination conditions over a common multi-agent coding substrate and includes concurrent-agent/conflict-resolution scenarios. It is a strong direct-S2 candidate, but the system-in-focus is multiple Claude agents plus a coordination condition and twining-mcp is not currently a canonical Index system.

cases.benchmark: DeepSeek Harness public benchmark entry point
cases.finding: Canonical Agent Teams exposes durable shared tasks/commitments and team coordination, but the public benchmark entry point currently directs users to the minimal jsonrpc-agent variant rather than the Agent Teams S2 path.

The benchmark holds model, prompts and tools constant across five framework implementations, but deliberately imposes the same Researcher-to-Analyst-to-Writer sequential pipeline. Its AutoGen path caps RoundRobinGroupChat at one round specifically to match that pipeline, so recurring inter-S1 interference is removed rather than exercised. Published quality, latency and token differences are not direct S2 evidence.

cases.benchmark: Astra cross-framework investment-team benchmark — Agno row
cases.finding: The Astra campaign is well matched at the model/tool/workload level, but its Agno organization is benchmark-authored: Agno 2.5.17 is configured as TeamMode.coordinate with a strict sequential analyst order and explicit benchmark instructions. This is not the canonical TeamMode.tasks mutual-adjustment path used to establish Agno S2, and the workload contains no explicit inter-S1 interference/attenuation disturbance. The published call/token/latency results therefore remain framework-execution evidence, not direct Agno.S2 capability evidence.

cases.benchmark: Astra cross-framework investment-team benchmark — AutoGen row
cases.finding: The Astra campaign runs AutoGen AgentChat 0.7.5 through first-party SelectorGroupChat, but the compared organization still uses a benchmark-authored selector prompt, custom all-analysts-spoken termination and workload-specific specialist topology. It does not expose a benchmark-defined inter-S1 interference/oscillation and its attenuation, so the matched cost/token/latency row cannot be promoted to a direct native S2 observation merely because canonical AutoGen establishes S2 elsewhere.

Canonical Squad now establishes S2=A, and the public MARBLE campaign evaluates Squad's first-party coordination path under controlled same-model/same-task factorial conditions, including coordination-only versus no-Squad and full-Squad versus memory-only contrasts. This is therefore native historical-lineage S2 capability evidence linked to canonical Squad. MARBLE still scores broad collaborative completion, milestone and judged-quality outcomes rather than an explicit inter-S1 interference/oscillation variable and its attenuation, so the result remains a native proxy rather than a direct S2 observation or primary baseline. Numeric results live only in the shared raw observation record.

MAO-Bench is structurally promising for native orchestration comparison: it defines parallel and sequential multi-agent tiers, adversarial failure/conflict tasks, topology/parallelism metrics, hermetic execution and an adapter interface. Its seeded leaderboard still has no published multi-orchestrator baseline results, so there is no matched canonical-harness S2 cell to admit or select yet.
